summary: Field report: Coach read a cm/360 increase (32.11 to 35.11) as sensitivity going up and the aim feeling faster. Root cause: three v8 sections wrote the lower-sensitivity experiment as 'lower cm/360' / 'lowering cm/360'. Physically, cm/360 is the centimeters of mouse travel per full 360-degree turn, so a larger value is a lower sensitivity; lowering sensitivity means raising cm/360 (cm/360 = 914.4 / (DPI x Horiz_Sens x yaw), and under Sens Scale 'cm/360' Horiz Sens is the cm/360 value itself, consistent along the whole chain). v9 corrects the three reversed phrasings and relocates the direction fact itself into the task-specific-sensitivity definition (see added_clarifications), so the direction is knowledge-base content served through the unified read entry point rather than a prompt rule. Entry set (37), schema (coach_knowledge_registry.v3), source_refs, claim_levels, and entry versions are unchanged, and every other cm/360 or sensitivity statement in v8 was re-audited for direction and left as is.
direction_rule: Larger cm/360 = lower sensitivity (low sens); smaller cm/360 = higher sensitivity (high sens). A lower-sensitivity experiment records a higher cm/360; pad spend per turn scales with cm/360.

corrected_entries.before: With overshoot confirmed and settings unchanged, run the existing single-variable sensitivity experiment: one recorded lower cm/360, a short familiarization block, then a matched retest.
corrected_entries.after: With overshoot confirmed and settings unchanged, run the existing single-variable sensitivity experiment: one recorded higher cm/360, a short familiarization block, then a matched retest.
corrected_entries.reason: The experiment motivated by this entry's definition is a lower-sensitivity one (cm/360 too fast to control), which is a higher cm/360 value. 'lower cm/360' literally described raising sensitivity and contradicted the same entry's definition.

corrected_entries.before: A long-unchanged sensitivity paired with persistent overshoot points at flick-force calibration rather than at reading or fatigue; lowering cm/360 shortens the distance each unit of force travels and can restore terminal control.
corrected_entries.after: A long-unchanged sensitivity paired with persistent overshoot points at flick-force calibration rather than at reading or fatigue; raising cm/360 (lowering sensitivity) shortens the distance each unit of force travels and can restore terminal control.
corrected_entries.reason: Reversed direction: lowering cm/360 raises sensitivity and lengthens the travel each unit of force produces, which worsens overshoot. Only raising cm/360 (a lower sensitivity) shortens the travel of a given force and restores terminal control.

corrected_entries.before: Community guidance conditions the reset habit: lower cm/360 spends more pad per turn, which makes frequent resets a genuine low-sensitivity requirement rather than a flaw, and the reset belongs in natural pauses between actions so the next flick never runs out of room.
corrected_entries.after: Community guidance conditions the reset habit: higher cm/360 spends more pad per turn, which makes frequent resets a genuine low-sensitivity requirement rather than a flaw, and the reset belongs in natural pauses between actions so the next flick never runs out of room.
corrected_entries.reason: Pad spent per full turn equals cm/360, so only a higher value (lower sensitivity) spends more pad and makes frequent resets a genuine low-sensitivity requirement; 'lower cm/360' contradicted the same sentence's low-sensitivity framing.

added_clarifications.before: There is no single perfect sensitivity independent of task, technique, and goal; cm/360 is a shared input-mapping unit.
added_clarifications.after: There is no single perfect sensitivity independent of task, technique, and goal; cm/360 is a shared input-mapping unit. It measures the mouse travel needed for a full 360-degree turn, so a larger value means lower and a smaller value means higher sensitivity.
added_clarifications.reason: The direction fact was first drafted as a prompt hard rule and rejected in review: it is domain knowledge and belongs in the registry so the unified knowledge read entry point serves it. Appended to this entry's definition, which already introduces cm/360 as the shared unit; source_refs and claim_level stay the entry's existing ones and no other field changes.

audited_unchanged.note: 'lower-sensitivity experiment' and 'at lower sensitivity' speak about sensitivity itself, not the cm/360 value; direction is correct and matches the fixed cue.
Hand speed demanded per degree scales linearly with cm/360: a larger value demands proportionally more hand travel. Mathematically correct; unchanged.
Scope and mechanism stay direction-neutral tradeoff framing; unchanged. The definition gained the direction sentence recorded under added_clarifications.
